key_bets: Spherical tokamak (A=2.3) geometry delivers higher beta that compensates for lower on-axis field (5.25 T) to achieve adequate fusion power density
REBCO HTS TF/PF coil system validated at Demo4 scale (11.8 T, 30 K, 7 MA-turns) scales to full ST-E1 (R=5.0 m) with ~32 cm center-stack shielding
Outboard-only liquid lithium metal blanket achieves TBR = 1.2 despite ~50% solid-angle coverage, providing tritium self-sufficiency
O-mode ECRH alone (no NBI, no ICRF) can sustain flat-top current drive for 15+ minute pulses in a burning plasma
WC-FeCr cermet center-stack shielding keeps fast neutron flux into the HTS core low enough (~1.4e17 m⁻² s⁻¹) to preserve REBCO lifetime
Quasi-steady pulsed operation (15+ min on / dwell off) with molten-salt thermal energy storage buffer delivers acceptable capacity factor for the grid
Burning-plasma Q high enough that 450–750 MWe net is achievable with ECRH-only auxiliary heating at tolerable recirculating power fraction
eliminated_costs: No beryllium supply chain exposure — liquid Li blanket avoids FLiBe's beryllium requirement
Lower REBCO tape performance requirements per unit length due to reduced on-axis field (5.25 T vs. 9.2 T for ARC), relaxing critical-current and mechanical-stress specs
No NBI or ICRF heating systems — ECRH-only flat-top removes NBI duct/first-wall integration, neutral-beam ion sources, and ICRF antenna hardware
FLiBe inventory and procurement cost avoided — liquid Li metal is commercially produced at battery scale and unconstrained relative to FLiBe
Reduced magnet-side mechanical structure mass relative to high-field compact tokamaks because lower B means lower Lorentz stress on the coil cage
novel_costs: Thermal energy storage buffer (molten salt) required to smooth pulsed ~15 min on / ~5 min off heat output to a steady grid — absent from steady-state designs
Dedicated WC-FeCr cermet center-stack neutron shield at nuclear-grade purity — a distinct capital and O&M line item with no equivalent in conventional aspect-ratio tokamaks
Li-6 enrichment capacity for high-enrichment liquid Li metal inventory, required to hit TBR=1.2 with only outboard coverage — limited global enrichment supply (Russia/China legacy processes)
Tritium extraction and permeation-barrier system specific to liquid Li metal circuit (vacuum degassing or permeation membranes) — different hardware than FLiBe extraction and unproven at plant scale
High ECRH recirculating power load from multi-tens of MW of gyrotrons at ~50–55% wall-plug efficiency, sized large because ECRH is the sole flat-top heating/current-drive source

risks.description: Q value, fusion power, and auxiliary heating power for ST-E1 are unpublished, leaving the LCOE anchor (≈1.5–2.5 GW fusion power estimate) resting on three unanchored assumptions
Power conversion cycle (steam Rankine vs. sCO₂ Brayton) not committed by Tokamak Energy; thermal efficiency assumption of ~33% is an analogue, and η_th elasticity on LCOE is −0.26
Outboard-only liquid Li blanket achieving TBR=1.2 is TRL 2–3; no fusion-scale demonstration of Li metal tritium extraction or TBR validation under realistic penetrations
WC-FeCr cermet center-stack shielding has no 14 MeV neutron irradiation database — explicitly flagged gap in Humphry-Baker & Smith (2019); REBCO lifetime under shielded flux unknown at ST-E1 scale

Capacity factor not published and pulsed operation with CS re-magnetization dwell periods pressures the low end of the 75–90% D-T MCF range; availability elasticity on LCOE is −0.87 (largest engineering lever)
No published capital cost estimate or plant study for ST-E1 Rev D; all CAS line items are framework defaults, and thermal buffer cost is not modelled (downward bias)
ECRH-only heating at ~50–55% wall-plug efficiency drives high recirculating power fraction; Q_engineering cannot be validated until auxiliary heating power is disclosed
Design has not stabilized — DPP 2024 to DPP 2025 showed dramatic change (85 MWe → 450–750 MWe net, R=4.25 → 5.0 m, A=2.0 → 2.3), indicating further parameter drift is plausible
REBCO tape global production (~few thousand km/year) insufficient for fleet scale; tape cost must fall from $30–100/kA-m toward ~$10/kA-m for commercial viability

Liquid Li metal chemical reactivity with air/water mandates fully inert-atmosphere primary circuit operations, and tritium permeation through steel heat exchangers from liquid Li is a documented (unsolved) concern
Li-6 enrichment supply chain dominated by Russia/China legacy mercury amalgam processes; Western capacity not at commercial scale for fusion demand
Global tritium inventory ~25–30 kg declining at 5.5%/year as CANDU reactors retire; ST-E1 startup inventory (~1 kg at >$35,000/g) shares the sequencing constraint of all D-T concepts
Fission-style regulatory treatment could apply a 2.2× building cost multiplier (Stewart & Shirvan 2022) to ST-E1 as a D-T plant
Remote maintenance for compact inboard center stack and outboard blanket modules in ST geometry is TRL 5–6 with no validated cycle time supporting the availability target

ST-E1 plasma current for Revision D not published (pre-Rev D value 13.6 MA at R=4.25 m); disruption loads on divertor and first wall during ramp-up/ramp-down of pulsed operation reduce effective availability
